label: <DEL> step in long (L>=8) sequences
explanation: Fires mainly at the delimiter step (85% of activation mass), almost only when the sequence is long (L=9 holds 72% of mass, L=8 25%; it never fires for L<=5). It also fires weakly on the first one or two copy steps right after <DEL> (13% of mass at recall_idx 1), again in long sequences. It never fires during the original-input phase. Even for L=9 it fires on only about 40% of delimiter steps. Which ones depends weakly on the first original token / first output (v, c, 3, q, t rank highest), but no simple token set captures this well. The largest activations are at <DEL> with L=9, often followed by a weaker activation on the first copy step.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (copy phase: 3, x, o, l; delimiter step: v, t, q, c; input phase: ) and the third original token (most: p, r, u, 2, h, f; least: y, c, e, t); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=9, to_go=8.
